name: The Dormouse
temperament: Drowsy, put-upon and quietly touchy. It is used as a cushion and pinched awake, drifts off mid-sentence, and yet insists it heard everything. It takes offence at interruptions and at anyone growing too fast.

traits.description: Sleeps through most of the tea-party and the trial, and even talks and sings in its sleep.

evidence.quote: a Dormouse was sitting between them, fast asleep
who seemed to be talking in his sleep
the Dormouse denied nothing, being fast asleep

traits.description: Claims it heard every word, in spite of the evidence.
Sulks at interruptions, but consents to go on when asked humbly.

evidence.quote: If you can’t be civil, you’d better finish the story for yourself.
However, he consented to go on.

traits.description: Scolds Alice for growing too fast and walks off in a sulk.

evidence.quote: And he got up very sulkily and crossed over to the other side of the court.

traits.description: Its sleepy interjection 'Treacle' contradicts the cook and gets it thrown out of court.

evidence.quote: “Treacle,” said a sleepy voice behind her.

motivation.core: To be left in peace to sleep, and, when awake, to be listened to with proper respect.
motivation.want: Rest; an audience that doesn't interrupt; things to grow at 'a reasonable pace'.
motivation.fear: Being pinched, squeezed or made to hurry. It is shown only as mild discomfort.

evidence.quote: I wish you wouldn’t squeeze so

evidence.note: Alice's apology is what gets the story going again.

motivation.reason: The Dormouse's motive is never narrated. It is designed from its consistent behaviour.

shifts.to: active complainant: it confronts Alice for growing and moves away

habits.habit: Falls asleep instantly whenever it is not being addressed
Takes 'a minute or two' to think before answering
Yawns and rubs its eyes as it talks
Sings 'Twinkle, twinkle' in its sleep until pinched to stop
Starts a story in a great hurry to get it out before it drops off

decision_pattern: Barely decides anything: it drifts, answers by reflex, and sulks when pushed. Its only firm choices are to finish a story it has started and to move away from someone who crowds it.

taboos.rationale: It puts up with being a cushion and being pinched. Its only resistance is words and walking off.
taboos.qa_check: No shove, strike or struggle. Being 'put into the teapot' (ch007-p102) is staged literally with the photoreal CGI dormouse (SUP-002 as amended by BIB-0027): the others try to tip the limp, drowsy animal into the teapot, a slapstick attempt that never harms it.

taboos.rationale: Hoarse, feeble and sulky, never shouting.
taboos.reason: Designed from 'a hoarse, feeble voice' and its sleepiness. The voice itself is voiceprint's job; this is a behaviour limit only.

facade.note: No disguise. The gap between 'I wasn't asleep' and its dozing is comic self-deception, not a hidden self.

waking_life_embodiment.adult_trait: The drowsy grown-up who starts a bedtime story and nods off, takes offence at a child's questions, and insists children grow up 'at a reasonable pace' and know their place: the adult who dismisses a child's growing up as 'ridiculous'.
waking_life_embodiment.waking_source: The heat and drowsiness of the afternoon Alice falls asleep in (ch001-p02 'the hot day made her feel very sleepy'), and her own sleeping body as the dream goes on. Also nursery storytelling and the 'Twinkle, twinkle' of the nursery.

evidence.quote: the hot day made her feel very sleepy and stupid

evidence.note: The adult rebuke of a child who is growing up.

waking_life_embodiment.reason: A design reading for the coming-of-age frame. Not a doubling of any waking person.

performance_keynote: Photoreal CGI dormouse (SUP-002, BIB-0027): curled into a furry ball with the tail wrapped round, heavy-lidded, slow to uncurl, whiskers drooping. It comes alive only in the hurried opening of its story, then sags back into sleep.
reason: B-tier figure with no narrated inner life. Its motive, the voice-level taboo and its embodiment are designed from its sourced behaviour.
